entries.title: bring the README up to date with the language
entries.body:
The feature table now lists the unsigned, f32 and ranged integer types,
enums, type aliases and discriminated unions, function-typed parameters,
Map and Set, switch, ?? and ?.-to-?? chains, nish/threads, calling C, and
capabilities with the no-panic scope. The standard library section names
the current modules (text, regex, YAML, SQLite, terminal, the full crypto
and networking stacks) instead of saying the language has no trim or
regular expression. The memory-safety table and the command-line section
follow the same changes.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: an idle keep-alive no longer makes every http1 expire walk every slot
entries.body: Http1Server.expire and Http1TlsServer.expire skip the slot walk until the soonest slot can be due, but Http1Connection.expiresNoSooner counted a head clock not yet started from the slot's last move. A kept-alive slot quiet past headTimeout put that bound in the past, so every expire walked every slot: about a third of a busy server's CPU at 30,000 connections a worker. expiresNoSooner now takes `now` and counts a clock not yet started from it. While an exchange is open it counts from lastActive instead, because nextRequest starts a pipelined head's clock there when the exchange ends. When slots close is unchanged. Security record H1-4.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: record where nish/net/postgres's client time goes
entries.body:
* perf(runtime): start nish/net/postgres's input buffer at 16 KiB

An 8 KiB buffer took a page of rows in two reads, and two epoll wakeups,
where libpq's 16 KiB takes one: strace on bench/postgres's list showed
5717 recvfrom for 3000 queries against libpq's 3028, and 3028 at 16 KiB.
Measurement against main is in progress; the figures follow in the PR.

Tests: tests/link/std_postgres

* docs(bench): record where nish/net/postgres's client time goes

Reverts the 16 KiB input buffer: it halves list's recvfrom and epoll_wait
calls but its CPU difference against main is inside the noise band on every
workload. The profile puts the module's own decoding at about 7.5 % of the
client's CPU on list, some 4 µs a query, under that workload's IQR, so no
decoding change is shipped; docs/BENCHMARKS.md records the profile, the
buffer experiment and its figures.

Measured: 16 KiB vs main, list +2.02 µs (band 2.06 µs), pk +0.09 µs (band 0.30), insert +0.86 µs (band 0.74); 12 rounds

* docs(bench): time the client's decoders, out of line and end to end

Re-profiles the PostgreSQL client with its decoders kept out of line, so
each shows its own self time. Times three decoder changes, in isolation and
against the noise band in 12 interleaved rounds. Corrects the buffer
table's reading against its band.

The walker change saves 18 ns a call, about 0.4 us a list query. That is
a quarter of the band, so no decoding change ships.

* docs(bench): record that the postgres client's loop has no system call to spare

strace counts one sendto, recvfrom and epoll_wait per answer and two
epoll_ctl a run, and halving list's reads did not move its CPU, so the
kernel's share is per-byte socket work and wakeups, not calls to cut.

* docs(bench): time on-demand input growth and every change together

A buffer that doubles to 64 KiB after a read fills it cuts list's reads
from 3,829 to 2,023, and with the three decoder changes measured 1.48 us
faster in one 12-round run and 2.63 us slower in the next. The copy's band
is about a tenth of a binary's run-to-run spread, so nothing ships.
